cohere_summary: Opera singer Liu Guijuan faced backlash after posting pictures of a headdress made from the feathers of 80 kingfishers, purchased for 120,000 yuan (£10,775). Conservationists and web users criticized her for disregarding animal welfare, with some calling for her to step down. While some defended her, citing industry rules and artistic tradition, others suggested using fake feathers instead. Liu initially defended her actions but later removed the post; two of China's 11 kingfisher species are protected, and police in Guangdong recently seized 60,000 dead kingfishers.

Ryanair and Aer Lingus engaged in another Twitter feud, exchanging jabs about their operations at Dublin Airport. Ryanair posted a promotional photo in Terminal 2, where Aer Lingus operates, prompting Aer Lingus to respond with a dig at Ryanair's use of smaller, less central airports. This follows a previous Twitter spat in January over Ryanair using an Aer Lingus plane in its promotional material. The rivalry occurs as the UK Court of Appeal prepares to rule on Ryanair's stake in Aer Lingus, which may force Ryanair to reduce its ownership due to competition regulations.

Bayern Munich's left-back David Alaba will miss the season's closing stages due to a torn knee ligament, sidelining him for around seven weeks. The injury occurred during Austria's 1-1 draw against Bosnia, marking his second significant knee injury this season. Alaba expressed disappointment but aims to return for the season finale. He had been instrumental in Bayern's pursuit of a treble, with the team currently leading the Bundesliga and advancing in the German Cup and Champions League.

Warren Weinstein, an American aid worker, was taken hostage by al Qaeda in 2011 and later killed in a U.S. anti-terror strike in January 2015. His family paid a ransom to his captors in 2012, but it did not secure his release, and the captors later demanded prisoner exchanges, including Dr. Aafia Siddiqui. The captors, who identified as "Afghans," maintained regular contact with a Pakistani source, boasting of connections to other terror events and threatening Weinstein's life. Despite efforts by Weinstein's family and Maryland lawmakers to secure his release, including meetings with U.S. and Pakistani officials, he was inadvertently killed in a drone strike, leading to emotional reactions from those involved in his case.

World No. 1 Novak Djokovic apologized to a ball boy he startled during a heated outburst at his support team in the Miami Open final against Andy Murray. Djokovic, frustrated after losing the second set, snatched a towel from the ball boy, prompting a code violation from the umpire. In a Facebook video, Djokovic expressed regret, emphasizing no intent to harm or scare the boy and extending his apology to the boy's parents. Despite the incident, Djokovic rallied to win the match 7-6, 4-6, 6-0, claiming his fifth Miami Open title.

Lazio secured a spot in the Coppa Italia final with a 1-0 win over Napoli, advancing 2-1 on aggregate, and will face Juventus on June 7. Defender Mauricio celebrated with fans using a selfie stick, while midfielder Senad Lulic, who scored the winning goal, expressed confidence in Lazio's chances against Juve. Lazio aims to extend their seven-game winning streak in Serie A when they host Empoli, sitting third in the standings, one point behind Roma. Juventus, meanwhile, reached the Coppa final with a 3-0 win over Fiorentina and plays Parma on Saturday.

Two 17-year-old teenagers, Jacob Polyakov and Jamal Maslow, were injured after sliding down the glass roof of the SEC 'Globe' shopping centre in Kiev, Ukraine, while intoxicated. Polyakov is in intensive care after hitting his head on stone steps, while Maslow broke his coccyx. Witnesses reported the boys were encouraged by friends to slide down the roof but quickly regretted it as they gained speed. Both were taken to the hospital, with Polyakov found unconscious and Maslow in severe pain.

The highly anticipated $300 million fight between Floyd Mayweather Jr. and Manny Pacquiao is set for May 2 at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Showtime released a promotional video showcasing Mayweather's training camp, highlighting his focus and dedication as he prepares for the bout. Mayweather, undefeated and nearing the welterweight limit, expressed his strong desire to win, calling it an "unbelievable match-up." Both fighters have been sharing their training progress on social media, with the fight for the WBA, WBO, and WBC welterweight titles just weeks away. Mayweather was within three-and-a-half pounds of the 147 lbs limit during a mandatory check 30 days before the fight.

Three friends, Steven Sloan, Michael Niccum, and Eugene Dight, encountered a pod of baby killer whales while crabbing off Anderson Island, Washington. Initially excited, they filmed the orcas swimming and jumping from a distance, but grew nervous as the whales approached their aluminum rowboat. Believing the sound of a rope being pulled attracted the orcas, the group panicked as one whale emerged close to the boat, with one member shouting, "We need to get out of here." The whales circled the boat, prompting nervous laughter and pleas from the group, who eventually rowed back to shore. Steven later shared the video, inviting viewers to laugh at their reaction and enjoy the orcas.

Scientists have developed a new cancer treatment technique that harnesses the body's immune system to target and kill cancerous cells in lung, skin, and bowel tumors. Early experiments on mice showed a 50% increase in survival rates, with the treatment "profoundly retarding" tumor growth. The method involves creating personalized vaccines based on an individual's tumor genetic makeup, boosting the immune system's T-cells to detect and destroy cancer cells. The first human clinical trial is set to begin with skin cancer patients, and experts believe this approach may provide a universal blueprint for targeting various human cancers.

A thief stole a sat nav from a 73-year-old woman's crashed car while she waited for an ambulance after colliding with railings in Hulme, Manchester. The woman, who suffered severe bruising, was with her husband, who has dementia, when the thief took the device from under the passenger seat. A member of the public photographed the suspect, described as a man aged 30-40 with a beard and wearing purple shorts, leaving the scene with his dog. Greater Manchester Police have issued the photograph and are appealing for anyone who recognizes the man to come forward. The victim described the thief as "the lowest of the low" in her statement.

Two armed robbers attempted to break into a jewellery shop in Pemberton, Wigan, using a sledgehammer and an axe, but were thwarted by a brave employee who barricaded the door. The raiders fled on a motorbike after being pushed back through a broken window, threatening a passer-by with the axe. Greater Manchester Police are investigating potential links to a similar break-in last week and have appealed for public assistance in identifying the offenders, commending the shop worker's bravery and a bystander who captured photos of the criminals. Anyone with information is urged to contact police or Crimestoppers.

A Loganair flight from Aberdeen to Shetland narrowly avoided crashing into the North Sea after being struck by lightning, which caused the autopilot to malfunction and send the plane into a nosedive. The pilot regained control just 1,100ft above the ocean, saving 30 passengers and three crew members. The incident occurred on December 15 during severe weather conditions, and the plane landed safely in Aberdeen with minor damage. An investigation by the AAIB found no technical faults with the aircraft, attributing the dive to the autopilot system countering the pilot's actions, and pilot training now includes simulations of the event.

A GoPro camera detached from a skydiver's helmet at 10,000 feet during a routine skydive in Everöd, Sweden, capturing its dizzying freefall to the ground. The camera spun uncontrollably for one and a half minutes before crashing into a field in Gringelstad, remarkably remaining intact. The footage, believed to be four years old, was found by Kristoffer Örstadius's father, who uploaded it to YouTube, leading to the owner's identification. The video has since amassed over 250,000 views, showcasing the camera's dramatic descent and survival.

A video captured at Whipsnade Zoo shows a young elephant breaking the single-file chain of its herd by walking alongside and then forcing its way back into the line. The baby elephant dawdles, picks something up with its trunk, and disrupts the tail-to-trunk connection between the last two elephants. The filmmaker described the scene as unexpected and amusing, highlighting the cheeky behavior of the young elephant. Whipsnade Zoo, located in Bedfordshire, is known for its large land area and diverse animal population.

Loren Mathieson filmed her Boston Terrier, Gizmo, walking on his front paws after trying on new booties, unsure how to walk in them. The video shows Gizmo taking steps forward, lifting his back legs vertically, and gracefully sidestepping. Mathieson’s laughter is heard as Gizmo eventually returns to all fours when he reaches her. The clip has been viewed over 80,000 times, bringing smiles to many viewers.

James Oliver, a convicted sex offender, was allegedly run over by his girlfriend, Linda Currier, after she caught him attempting to sexually assault a 12-year-old girl in Noblesboro, Maine. The incident occurred on Saturday night, resulting in a serious leg injury for Oliver. Currier was arrested for operating under the influence and aggravated assault, while Oliver was later charged with attempted gross sexual assault, unlawful sexual touching, and failing to comply with the sex offender registration act. Oliver, previously convicted of sexual abuse of a minor and rape, was transferred to a state prison pending a court appearance.

A skateboarder, Jared Henry, collided with a deer while filming a video at 40mph in the Ozark Mountains. The deer died from a broken pelvis, while Henry escaped unharmed. Henry later expressed relief at surviving the incident and shared his experience on Facebook. The video has garnered over 300,000 views, with viewers noting Henry's fortunate escape.

Middlesbrough suffered a 2-0 away defeat to Watford, with goals from Troy Deeney and Odion Ighalo, losing their Championship lead. Defensive errors and a lack of creativity contributed to Middlesbrough's poor performance, marking their fourth loss in five away games. Watford's strikers, Deeney and Ighalo, were praised for their effectiveness, with Deeney reaching 20 goals for the season and Ighalo scoring his 19th. Middlesbrough manager Aitor Karanka expressed pride in his team's overall season but acknowledged the need to improve, while Watford manager Slavisa Jokanovic highlighted the importance of the win for their promotion push.

Cody, a horse, got stuck in a muddy bog in Belvedere, south-east London, on Friday afternoon. Animal rescue experts and fire crews worked for over an hour to free the distressed animal, who was covered in mud but unharmed. The rescue operation began shortly before 1:30 pm and ended at 2:55 pm. Cody was taken back to the stables to be examined by a vet. Borough Commander Richard Welch confirmed the horse's safety and joked about its unlikely participation in the Grand National.

A pair of Arctic foxes engaged in a deadly fight over a vixen on a snowy Iceland mountainside, captured by wildlife photographer Einar Gudmann. The battle began when a third fox interrupted a mating pair, leading to a vicious struggle that tumbled down to a rocky beach. One fox gained a dominant bite, forcing the other into the sea, and the wet, wounded loser was not expected to survive the night. The victorious fox searched for the vixen, who had fled to the mountainside, while the defeated fox struggled to escape, likely facing its final night.

Mary Kay Letourneau Fualaau, a former teacher who served over seven years in prison for having a sexual relationship with her 13-year-old student, Vili Fualaau, is now 53 and still married to him. They will celebrate their 10th wedding anniversary on May 20 and have two teenage daughters together. In an upcoming ABC "20/20" interview, the couple discusses their marriage, Letourneau's plans to teach again and have her sex offender status lifted, and Fualaau's struggles with alcoholism and depression. Letourneau was 34 when the relationship began, and Fualaau is now 31.

Susie Clark found a 3.69-carat white diamond, the largest this year, at Crater of Diamonds State Park in Arkansas after praying for a gem. She named it the Hallelujah Diamond and plans to keep it. The park, the only public diamond-digging site globally, allows visitors to retain their finds. Over 75,000 diamonds have been discovered since 1906, with the largest being the 40.23-carat Uncle Sam found in 1924. Park staff regularly plow the field to bring more diamonds to the surface for visitors.

Quinn Patrick, on a fishing trip with his dad at Snow Lake, Indiana, was surprised when a seemingly lifeless bowfin fish suddenly propelled itself from the ground and slapped him in the face with its tail. The incident, captured on video, included a cartoon-like sound effect upon impact, causing Quinn to recoil in shock while his dad laughed, eventually prompting Quinn to laugh along. After noticing blood on the fish, Quinn expressed concern, but his dad reassured him that the fish was hurt before they caught it. The video concluded with the father discussing the size of the bowfin’s teeth, and the article provided additional information about bowfin, a demersal freshwater fish native to North America.

Paul Gregory, 51, from Bedford, was fined £795 and ordered to perform 150 hours of unpaid work for dishonestly obtaining a blue badge by claiming he could only walk 200 metres, despite being a keen walker and member of a mountaineering club. He was exposed when council officials discovered a newspaper article detailing his 191-mile hike and another weekend walking trip in Wales. Gregory pleaded guilty to two counts of misrepresenting his physical abilities at Luton Magistrates' Court. Bedford Borough Council described the case as one of the most outrageous instances of blue badge fraud they had investigated.

A 23-year-old man has been arrested and bailed in connection with the death of Vanessa Santillan, a 33-year-old transgender escort found strangled and beaten in a Fulham flat in March. Santillan, a Mexican national working in London, Paris, and Miami, died from head and neck injuries. Scotland Yard is appealing for information about her final hours, emphasizing they will do 'everything' to solve the case. Detective Chief Inspector Rebecca Reeves urged anyone who saw Santillan on the days before her death to come forward.

Edinson Cavani, PSG's striker, visited a zoo after a disappointing 2-0 defeat to Barcelona, where he struggled to perform. The 28-year-old posed for pictures with various animals, including goats, bears, and llamas. Despite scoring 18 goals this season, Cavani's performance has been questioned by the media, and his future at the club is uncertain, with Manchester United reportedly monitoring his situation. Cavani, however, has expressed his desire to stay at PSG for the duration of his contract.

Tesla founder Elon Musk has unveiled the Powerwall, a $3,000 home battery that can power a house for eight hours, storing electricity at night when rates are cheaper. The device, available in 7kWh and 10kWh versions, can be installed on an interior or exterior wall and used for daily energy needs or as emergency backup power. Musk claims the technology could revolutionize energy use, allowing homeowners to store renewable energy and reduce reliance on the grid. Tesla also introduced the Powerpack, a scalable system for businesses and utilities, aiming to transform the global energy infrastructure to zero carbon.

Burglars caused extensive damage to a family home in Hatfield Peverel, Essex, flooding the kitchen, slashing furniture, and stealing valuable items including jewellery, electronics, and sentimental heirlooms. The intruders also left behind signs of their presence, such as bread and butter on the sideboard, and caused thousands of pounds in damage. The victim described the scene as "mindless destruction," and Detective Constable Nick Campbell called it one of the worst examples of vandalism he has seen in his career. The police are determined to catch the perpetrators before they strike again.

Kayonna Cole, an exotic pet owner from Los Angeles, calmly allowed her pet tarantula, a female rose hair spider, to bite her hand while filming. The video shows the spider digging its fangs into her skin, with Kayonna remaining unflinching despite the spider's aggressive behavior. Later, she experienced a reaction to the venom, describing symptoms like redness, soreness, and itching, but noted the tarantula's venom is low toxicity, similar to a bee sting. Cole shared that the spider might have been testing its fangs or showing aggression during the incident.

The Research Vessel Flip (RV Flip), a 355-foot scientific platform, has been used by the US Office for Naval Research for over 50 years. It lacks an engine and is towed to its destination, where it flips 90 degrees, leaving only 50 feet above the surface, providing exceptional stability for research. The vessel uses ballast tanks to shift its center of gravity, completing the flip in 20 minutes. It accommodates five crew and eleven researchers for up to 30 days, conducting studies in underwater acoustics, oceanography, meteorology, and marine mammal observation. Launched in 1962, it was initially vital for submarine development during the Cold War and has since been used for marine life and weather research.

John Bramblitt, who lost his sight 12 years ago due to epilepsy, has developed a unique painting technique using touch. He uses fabric paint with raised edges to create outlines and different textured paints to fill in colors, based on a mental image. Bramblitt's method allows him to produce highly accurate paintings, including one of his guide dog, which he has never seen. His artwork has gained recognition, and he sells limited edition prints and originals, fostering connections and optimism for his future.

Researchers at Vanderbilt University found that children's soft toys can harbor bacteria, potentially increasing the risk of surgical-site infections. Their study revealed that all tested toys showed bacterial growth, but a simple wash and dry cycle followed by sealing in a plastic bag sterilized 79% of them. The team urged parents to clean their child's toys before bringing them into the operating room to minimize infection risks. Future studies will explore the correlation between bacteria on toys and surgical infections, as well as the impact of providing sterile toys.

Premier League leaders Chelsea host a resurgent Manchester United on Saturday, with both teams having high stakes in the match. United, currently in top form, are aiming for a Champions League spot, while Chelsea seeks to solidify their title bid. Key players like Angel di Maria and Juan Mata are in focus, with Mata's recent success at United contrasting Di Maria's slump. A United victory could significantly impact the title race, potentially narrowing the gap with Chelsea and increasing pressure on the Blues. The match also features managerial egos clashing between Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal.

Researchers from the New Jersey Institute of Technology, led by Dr. Haimin Wang, have captured the first high-resolution footage of solar flux ropes, revealing their twisting magnetic fields and formation process. The video shows an S-shaped bundle of magnetic fields evolving into a multi-stranded flux rope, accompanied by a solar flare. These structures, common in the solar corona, are believed to cause solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs), impacting space weather and potentially damaging satellites, airlines, and electricity grids. The study, published in *Nature Communications*, aims to enhance understanding of flux rope formation and their role in solar eruptions.

Manchester United's Wayne Rooney sustained a knee injury during their 3-0 defeat to Everton on Sunday, being replaced by Robin van Persie in the 88th minute. Manager Louis van Gaal confirmed the injury but stated it was too early to determine its severity. The loss marked United's first back-to-back league defeats under Van Gaal, leaving them fourth in the race for Champions League qualification, with Liverpool now applying pressure. The injury adds to a miserable afternoon for United, who saw Everton climb into the top half of the table.

As the world awaits the birth of William and Kate's second child, speculation about potential names is rampant, with many believing the couple is expecting a princess. If a girl, she will be the first Princess of Cambridge born into the royal family in 182 years, making her birth historically significant due to recent changes in succession laws. While "Diana" is a popular choice among the public, the author argues against it, citing the divisive nature of Diana's legacy and the potential burden it would place on the child. The author suggests that William honors his mother's memory through his actions as a husband and father, rather than by naming his child after her, and proposes alternative names like Alice, Elizabeth, Victoria, Charlotte, or Alexandra.

Misty Machinshok, 33, was jailed for 15 to 30 years for convincing her husband, Gary Machinshok, to repeatedly rape her 15-year-old daughter in an attempt to conceive a child, as she is infertile. She coached the pair on positions to conceive and held her daughter's hand during the initial assaults. Gary Machinshok pleaded no contest to raping the teenager and sexually assaulting her 11-year-old sister, with both victims now in foster care. The crime was exposed when a friend of the older girl alerted a teacher, who then called the police. Misty Machinshok pleaded guilty to multiple charges, including rape and child endangerment, to protect her daughter from testifying.

High street retailers like Debenhams and Mothercare are abandoning prolonged sales in favor of shorter, more impactful promotions, leading to improved financial results. Experts argue that continuous sales devalue products and train shoppers to wait for discounts, harming profits. Debenhams has reduced sale days by 39 in the past year, focusing on better initial pricing, while Mothercare has shortened its Christmas sales from eight weeks to three. Retail analysts support this shift, stating that constant discounting erodes margins and becomes a self-perpetuating cycle. Both companies report positive customer feedback and stabilized margins since implementing these changes.

A worker in Greenwich, south east London, was photographed jet washing a roof 30 feet above the ground with only a rope tied around him for safety. A local resident reported the incident, expressing disbelief at the lack of proper safety equipment. A building expert criticized the setup, stating the worker should have had scaffolding and a harness. The Health and Safety Executive (HSE) intervened, serving a prohibition notice to halt the work until appropriate safety measures are implemented.

Tom Brady publicly expressed his admiration and love for his wife, Gisele Bundchen, on Facebook as she retired from runway modeling after 20 years in the industry. Bundchen, the highest-paid model in 2014, announced her retirement to focus on family and special projects. Brady praised her determination and beauty, calling her the "love of my life" and using hashtags #GOAT and #thebestisyettocome. The couple, married since 2009 with two children, will now spend more quality time together.

Scientists from the University of East Anglia warn that the growing demand for rubber, primarily driven by the tyre industry, is causing significant deforestation, with up to 21 million acres of jungle expected to be cleared for rubber plantations by 2024. This expansion threatens endangered species in Southeast Asia, including gibbons, leopards, and elephants, as well as protected areas like the Snoul Wildlife Sanctuary in Cambodia. The study, published in Conservation Letters, highlights that 70% of natural rubber is consumed by the tyre industry, leading to biodiversity loss and the decline of various animal species in affected forests.

Adam Peaty, a 20-year-old British swimmer, broke the men's 100-meter breaststroke world record with a time of 57.92 seconds at the London Aquatic Centre, surpassing Cameron van der Burgh's 2012 record of 58.46 seconds. Peaty expressed delight in his achievement, crediting his hard work and training. In other events, Ben Proud won the men's 50m freestyle, Fran Halsall secured her 10th consecutive title in the women's 50m freestyle, and Rachael Kelly defended her British Championship title in the 100m butterfly.

A nine-year-old boy in Nanjing, China, was severely abused by his adoptive mother, who whipped him with skipping ropes, metal rods, and water pipes for not knowing the story of Pinocchio. The abuse was discovered by his school six months ago, but it was only recently reported to authorities after his injuries worsened and he became withdrawn. The adoptive mother, Li, was arrested on suspicion of child abuse, and the boy has been returned to his biological parents. Photographs of his injuries sparked widespread outrage online, and psychologists have been enlisted to support the child.

Jondrew Lachaux, 39, allegedly impregnated his 17-year-old stepdaughter, who gave birth alone at home while caring for her three-year-old sister, who later died. Lachaux and the teen's mother, Kellie Phillips, left the girls behind during a six-month road trip, providing insufficient food and medication. The teen, suffering from malnutrition, gave birth without medical assistance and later faced charges of child abuse and concealing evidence. Lachaux was arrested on charges of child abuse and concealing evidence, while Phillips also faces child abuse charges, and their five other children are now in protective services. The 17-year-old stepdaughter also faces charges, with the district attorney questioning whether she should be punished or receive treatment.

A section of the M25 motorway in Kent was closed due to a serious motorcycle accident, causing significant traffic delays. During the closure, some motorists exited their vehicles to play football on the carriageway, prompting a warning from Kent Police about the dangers of leaving vehicles in stationary traffic. Additionally, two teenagers who had crossed the motorway during the closure were stranded when the road reopened and required police assistance to return to their vehicle. The incident followed another serious event in Kent where a coach caught fire on an A2 slip road, causing significant damage.

A silver Mercedes driver attempted to undertake traffic on the M58 near Switch Island in Merseyside to avoid a queue. A Renault driver blocked the Mercedes by pulling into the inside lane, preventing it from advancing. The Mercedes driver tried repeatedly to overtake and undertake the Renault, but the Renault driver swerved to block each attempt. The confrontation lasted over a minute, with both drivers shouting and pointing at each other. Eventually, the Mercedes driver was forced to wait in the queue like everyone else, and the incident was captured on dashcam and shared on YouTube, quickly gaining thousands of views.

A Saudi Arabian citizen, Mohammed Mohsen, captured footage of a powerful sandstorm sweeping across a street, engulfing everything in its path. The storm caused significant disruption in Saudi Arabia and neighboring countries, leading to flight cancellations, school closures, and car crashes. Strong winds and reduced visibility were reported, with the storm spreading across the Arabian Peninsula into the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Yemen. Despite sandstorms being common in the region, this one was unusually large and destructive, prompting many to share their experiences and images on social media.

Randy Johnston, a 68-year-old grandfather from Dallas, Texas, played an April Fool's prank on his granddaughters by leaving fake poop on their beds, which was filmed by his son. The prank backfired when his six-year-old granddaughter, Porter, reacted with horror and tears, mistaking the fake poop for real. Porter's father tried to console her, explaining it was a joke, but she remained upset. Randy revealed he staged the prank in retaliation for a previous joke his granddaughters played on him, filling his office with stuffed animals. The incident highlights the potential for pranks to go awry, even within families with a history of practical jokes.

Italian artist Johannes Stoetter created a remarkable illusion by painting two female models to resemble a chameleon, using water-based body paint and intertwining them to form the creature's shape. The intricate piece, titled *The Chameleon*, took four days to design and six hours to paint, with the models resting on a matching bench and holding a green branch to complete the effect. Stoetter, known for transforming models into animals like frogs and parrots, draws inspiration from nature and everyday life, though his artworks exist only briefly before being washed off. The artist reflects that body painting teaches the impermanence of art and intensifies its appreciation.
